rule: A person domiciled in China, or a person without domicile who stays in China for at least 183 days in a tax year, is treated as a resident individual. A nonresident is taxed on China-source income under the law.
application: A U.S. passport alone does not determine China tax residence; domicile and days must be assessed.

sources.label: China Individual Income Tax Law (official English translation)

item: Individual income tax categories and headline rates
rule: Law lists comprehensive income (including salary and wages) at progressive rates of 3–45%; business-operation income at 5–35%; interest/dividends, asset rental, asset transfer and incidental income at 20%.
application: Statutory category rates only; they do not establish that a conversion or transfer is taxable or compute tax on this account. Deductions, exemptions, residency and income classification matter.

sources.label: China Individual Income Tax Law (official English translation)

rule: Equivalent USD 50,000 per person/year is an ID-only facilitation threshold for specified settlement and domestic-individual FX purchases. SAFE separately says overseas individuals holding a Chinese foreign permanent-residence ID are eligible for the purchase quota; it is not a universal limit.
application: Not a tax and not permission to split transactions or use another person’s quota. Confirm the account holder’s SAFE classification and any permanent-residence ID.
status: official SAFE guidance; category and bank processing need confirmation

sources.label: SAFE 2025 FAQ on quota eligibility for foreign permanent-residence ID holders

rule: U.S. citizens generally must report worldwide income. Moving existing principal is analytically distinct from earning income; the underlying source and any interest, dividends, wages or gains need separate classification.
application: Prior U.S. income-tax reporting cannot be checked without source, years, records and filed returns.
status: official rule; personal tax due unverified

rule: The Code treats disposition of nonfunctional currency as a §988 transaction; personal-transaction rules include a no-recognition rule for currency gain only when the otherwise recognized gain does not exceed USD 200.
amount: USD 200 threshold for the specified personal-transaction no-gain rule
application: Not a blanket exemption for income or interest. Basis, acquisition date, transaction, and personal/business classification are needed.

rule: Only a legal, actual qualifying foreign income-tax liability paid/accrued may potentially qualify; credits are limited and refundable foreign taxes are not tax legally owed.
application: This may reduce U.S. double taxation on qualifying foreign income, not bank conversion spreads, wire costs, or other charges.
status: official IRS guidance; taxpayer facts unknown

rule: A U.S. person with financial interest or signature/other authority over foreign accounts generally files when aggregate value of reportable accounts exceeded USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year.
amount: USD 10,000 aggregate at any time during year
application: Information reporting; separate from income tax. Prior-year filing history is unknown.
status: official IRS guidance; filing status unverified

rule: Separate asset-reporting requirement may apply to specified U.S. taxpayers; threshold depends on filing status and whether living in the U.S. or abroad. It does not replace FBAR.
application: Need tax filing status, residence and asset balances; no threshold is inferred for this person.
status: official IRS guidance; filing status unverified
